plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their behavior. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. Since my value is $3, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $3, ensuring I only win when profitable (paying less than $3) and never overpay.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid (not my own bid) if I win, there's no incentive to bid above or below my true value of $31. Bidding higher risks winning and paying more than the item is worth to me if I'm the second-highest bidder's price exceeds my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of others' strategies.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy: you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid (profitable), and you never pay more than your value. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth, while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior round history to adjust for, the theoretically optimal and safest strategy is to bid exactly my private value of $32.
